item.title: Shiraito Falls: A Curtain of Fuji Spring Water — Guide
item.description: Shiraito Falls, near Fujinomiya at the southwestern foot of Mount Fuji, is one of Japan’s most graceful waterfalls, its name meaning ‘white threads’ after the hundreds of silky streams of water that pour over a curved, 20-metre-high and 150-metre-wide cliff face. Almost all of the water is Mount Fuji’s rain and snowmelt, filtered through the volcanic rock for decades before emerging from the cliff itself, and the falls are a component site of Fuji’s World Heritage listing, long revered as a place of worship and purification.
